title: Reconcile inference portability with Hardware Fabric, HRB execution paths, Unified Action Fabric, AI communication topology and current provider releases
decisions: The global hardware baseline remains vendor-neutral and valid with zero accelerators; provider-specific CUDA, SM, GPU SKU, ROCm, Level Zero and NPU details remain provider-scoped compatibility evidence.
Accelerator inference requires a discovered DEVICE-bound available compatible execution backend and an HRB lease binding the exact execution path; physical device presence alone is insufficient.
Backend disappearance or topology revalidation failure invalidates the affected lease and reuse of derived engine/runtime-cache artifacts until re-admission.
The Model Router remains the logical model/provider/runtime routing authority; inference portability performs backend eligibility, compilation, execution and evidence only.
Agent Native inference must enter through a typed Unified Action Fabric action and cannot directly bypass Model Router, HRB, security policy or the provider adapter.
Execution providers/backends are not AI participants and backend selection/fallback cannot expand an application's closed AI communication participant set.
Decision Fabric/Jev may only advise within a deterministically prefiltered eligible candidate set, may not add candidates and never becomes routing/resource/security authority.

OpenVINO 2026.4.0, ONNX Runtime 1.30.0, TensorRT 11.3.0.99/CUDA 13.4, TensorRT-RTX 1.6.1.120 and TensorRT-RTX EP ABI 0.4.2 are pinned compatibility references only, not automatic production promotion.
